preamble: Delateralization of the voiceless lateral fricative [ɬ] to the postalveolar [ʃ]. Proto-Semitic *ś (s2), reconstructed as [ɬ], became Arabic šīn (ش) — Arabic š comes from *ś, while Proto-Semitic *š merged with s — and in Akkadian and Ugaritic *ś merged with š. Hebrew, Aramaic and Ethiopian Semitic took the other path, to [s].

examples.note: Ugaritic likewise writes the reflex of *ś with š.

sources: Huehnergard, J. (2004). Afro-Asiatic. In R. D. Woodard (ed.), The Cambridge Encyclopedia of the World's Ancient Languages. Cambridge University Press.
